description: Imagine sinking your teeth into a slice of authentic Focaccia Genovese, a Ligurian masterpiece renowned for its crisp exterior and incredibly soft, airy interior. This beloved Italian bread is generously infused with fragrant rosemary and the finest extra virgin olive oil, creating an irresistible aroma and a truly unforgettable taste experience. Perfect as an appetizer, a side to a meal, or a delightful snack on its own, it embodies the simple elegance of Italian baking.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Pour in 30ml of the extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms and all ingredients are well combined.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface. Knead for 10-15 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. If using a stand mixer, knead with a dough hook for 8-10 minutes until it passes the windowpane test.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly grease a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turn to coat, then cover with a clean kitchen towel or plastic wrap. Let it rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size. This is crucial for flavor development.

instructions.title: Prepare for Baking
instructions.text: Gently punch down the risen dough and transfer it to a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan generously coated with 20ml of olive oil. Using your fingertips, gently stretch the dough to fill the pan. Dimple the surface of the focaccia deeply with your fingers, creating small wells.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Preheat
instructions.text: Drizzle the top of the focaccia with a little more olive oil, then sprinkle with fresh rosemary leaves and coarse sea salt. Cover the pan again and let the focaccia rise for another 30-45 minutes in a warm place. Meanwhile, preheat your oven to 220C (425F).

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Bake the focaccia in the preheated oven for 25-35 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. The crust should be crisp and the interior soft and airy. Keep an eye on it to prevent over-browning.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Once out of the oven, immediately drizzle generously with the remaining extra virgin olive oil. This adds incredible flavor and shine. Let it cool slightly in the pan before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely, then slice and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: For an even more authentic texture and flavor, use high-quality Italian 00 flour. It yields a finer crumb and better elasticity.
Do not skimp on the olive oil! It is fundamental to the Genovese focaccia's characteristic crisp crust, soft interior, and rich flavor. Use a good extra virgin olive oil.
Focaccia is best enjoyed fresh on the day it is baked. If you have leftovers, reheat them briefly in a warm oven (around 150C/300F) for 5-7 minutes to restore its delightful texture.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast of Italy, where the salty breeze carries the irresistible aroma of freshly baked focaccia. Among the myriad of Italian breads, Focaccia Genovese stands out as a true masterpiece – a testament to simplicity, quality ingredients, and a rich baking tradition. This iconic flatbread, celebrated for its dimpled surface, ethereal crumb, and generous anointing of extra virgin olive oil and fragrant rosemary, is more than just bread; it's an experience. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating that authentic taste of Italy in your own kitchen, learning the classic Focaccia Genovese recipe is your first delicious step. Get ready to discover the secrets behind this beloved Italian staple, from its humble origins to the step-by-step process that transforms simple ingredients into an unforgettable delight.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?
Focaccia Genovese, or Fûgassa in the local Ligurian dialect, is the quintessential flatbread from Genoa, the capital city of Italy's Liguria region. Unlike its thicker, often more bread-like counterparts found elsewhere in Italy, the Genovese version is typically thinner, incredibly airy, and boasts a uniquely crispy, golden crust thanks to its liberal application of olive oil. Its signature characteristic is the pattern of deep dimples pressed into its surface, which act as small reservoirs for a luscious olive oil and water emulsion, ensuring every bite is moist and flavorful.

Historically, focaccia was a humble baker's bread, often baked in the morning to test the oven's temperature before baking larger loaves. Its name derives from the Latin "focus," meaning "hearth" or "fireplace," highlighting its ancient origins. What makes Focaccia Genovese particularly special is its emphasis on high-quality extra virgin olive oil, fine sea salt, and often, fresh rosemary. It's designed to be enjoyed at any time of day – for breakfast with coffee, as a snack, or alongside meals. Its delicate balance of chewiness and crispness, combined with the intoxicating aroma of rosemary and rich olive oil, makes it an irresistible example of Ligurian baking at its finest.

## Ingredients for Focaccia Genovese
The beauty of the Focaccia Genovese recipe lies in its simplicity, relying on a few high-quality ingredients to achieve extraordinary flavor and texture. Sourcing the best possible components is crucial for an authentic result.

Here’s what you’ll need:
*   **High-Quality Bread Flour:** '00' flour is traditional for a very fine crumb, but a good strong bread flour with high protein content will also yield excellent results, providing the necessary gluten structure.
*   **Active Dry Yeast or Instant Yeast:** Essential for the rise and airy texture.
*   **Warm Water:** Around 105-115°F (40-46°C) for activating the yeast.
*   **Sugar:** A pinch helps to wake up the yeast.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** Incorporated into the dough for flavor.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil (EVOO):** This is non-negotiable. Use a high-quality, flavorful EVOO, as it's not just an ingredient but a star of the show, used in the dough, for oiling the pan, and as a generous topping.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Sprigs of fresh rosemary are pressed into the dimples, infusing the focaccia with its signature aromatic notes.
*   **Flaky Sea Salt:** For sprinkling over the top before baking, providing a delightful textural contrast and burst of salty flavor.

Remember, the quality of your olive oil and freshness of your rosemary will profoundly impact the final taste of your Focaccia Genovese. Don't skimp on these vital elements!

## How to Make Focaccia Genovese: Step-by-Step
Mastering the Focaccia Genovese recipe is a rewarding process that involves patience and a love for Italian baking. Follow these steps for an authentic taste of Liguria:

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water, sugar, and yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Pour in about 2-3 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
3.  **Knead (or No-Knead):** For a traditional approach, transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it's smooth and elastic. Alternatively, for a no-knead method, simply cover the bowl and let the gluten develop over a longer first rise. The dough should be quite sticky – don't add too much extra flour.
4.  **First Rise:** Lightly oil a clean bowl with EVOO, place the dough in it, and turn to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Generously coat a 9x13-inch (or similar size) baking sheet with extra virgin olive oil. Don't be shy; this oil contributes to the focaccia's crispy bottom and rich flavor.
6.  **Shape the Dough:** Gently transfer the risen dough to the oiled baking sheet. Using oiled hands, carefully stretch and press the dough to fill the pan, trying not to deflate it too much. If the dough resists, let it rest for 10 minutes, then continue stretching.
7.  **Dimple the Dough:** Once the dough covers the pan, use your fingertips to create deep, characteristic dimples all over the surface. Press down firmly but not all the way through the dough.
8.  **Second Rise:** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a clean towel and let the focaccia rise again for another 30-45 minutes in a warm place. The dough should look visibly puffier.
9.  **Prepare the Brine/Topping:** In a small bowl, whisk together 3 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil, 2 tablespoons of water, and a pinch of fine sea salt until emulsified.
10. **Top and Bake:** Drizzle the olive oil-water mixture generously over the dimpled focaccia, ensuring it pools in the indentations. Press fresh rosemary sprigs into some of the dimples, and sprinkle flaky sea salt evenly over the entire surface.
11. **Bake:** Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and the bottom is crisp and golden.
12. **Cool and Serve:** Once out of the oven, for an extra touch, you can drizzle a little more fresh EVOO over the hot focaccia. Let it cool on a wire rack for a few minutes before slicing and serving.

## Tips for Perfect Focaccia Genovese
Achieving that perfect Focaccia Genovese recipe result requires attention to a few key details:

*   **Embrace High Hydration:** The dough for Focaccia Genovese is quite wet and sticky. Don't be tempted to add too much extra flour, as this high hydration is what contributes to its incredibly airy and tender crumb.
*   **Quality Olive Oil is King:** We cannot stress this enough. The flavor of your extra virgin olive oil will shine through, so invest in a good bottle. It contributes to both flavor and texture.
*   **Generous Oiling:** Don't hold back on the olive oil when preparing the pan and drizzling the top. It's essential for achieving that signature crispy bottom and rich, moist interior.
*   **Patience with Proofing:** Allow ample time for both rises. Proper proofing ensures a light, airy texture and better flavor development. A warm, draft-free environment is ideal.
*   **Hot Oven, Fast Bake:** Baking at a high temperature helps to create a beautiful golden crust quickly while keeping the interior soft and moist.
*   **Don't Overwork the Dough:** After the first rise, handle the dough gently to preserve the air bubbles that have formed. This is especially true when stretching it into the pan and dimpling.

## Serving Suggestions for Focaccia Genovese
The beauty of Focaccia Genovese lies in its versatility. While utterly delicious on its own, especially when fresh from the oven, it also serves as a fantastic accompaniment to a variety of dishes.

*   **Appetizer:** Serve it with a simple bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping, or alongside balsamic vinegar. It's also excellent with antipasti platters, cured meats, and cheeses.
*   **Accompaniment:** Focaccia Genovese is the perfect partner for hearty soups, fresh salads, or any Italian meal where you'd typically serve bread. Its robust flavor stands up well to rich sauces.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill it with your favorite sandwich ingredients – prosciutto, mozzarella, roasted vegetables, or pesto for a truly gourmet experience.
*   **Breakfast/Snack:** In Liguria, it's common to enjoy focaccia with a morning coffee, or as a simple snack throughout the day. Its subtle sweetness and savory notes make it surprisingly versatile.

## Focaccia Genovese Variations & Substitutions
While the classic rosemary and olive oil Focaccia Genovese recipe is perfect as is, you can explore delicious variations to suit your taste or what you have on hand.

*   **Other Toppings:** Before baking, consider adding other traditional Ligurian toppings. Thinly sliced onions (caramelized or fresh), cherry tomatoes (pressed into the dimples), or pitted black olives are popular choices.
*   **Herbs:** While rosemary is classic, you can experiment with other fresh herbs like thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano can be added during the last 5-10 minutes of baking for a cheesy crust.
*   **Flour Alternatives:** While '00' flour or bread flour is recommended, you can experiment with a portion of whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor and denser texture, though it won't be as traditional. For gluten-free options, a good quality gluten-free bread blend can be used, but the texture will differ significantly.
*   **No-Knead Method:** If you prefer less hands-on time, a no-knead version of this Focaccia Genovese recipe simply requires a longer initial proofing (8-12 hours or overnight in the fridge) with minimal mixing, letting time do the work of gluten development.

Baking Focaccia Genovese is more than just following a recipe; it's an act of culinary love, connecting you to centuries of Italian tradition. The aroma filling your kitchen, the satisfying dimpling of the dough, and the first bite of that perfectly crisp, yet impossibly soft bread—these are the moments that make homemade Italian baking so special. Don't hesitate to try this Focaccia Genovese recipe; you'll be rewarded with a truly unforgettable taste of Italy.
